sourceEvidence.claim: HALLMARK 1 — Growth signal self-sufficiency: mutations in genes encoding proto-oncogenes (↑ growth factors, autocrine loop, eg, ↑PDGF in brain tumors); growth factor receptors (constitutive signaling, eg, HER2 in breast cancer); signaling molecules (eg, RAS); transcription factors (eg, MYC); cell cycle regulators (eg, cyclins, CDKs)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Growth signal
self-sufficiency

Mutations in genes encoding:
▘ Proto-oncogenes → ↑ growth factors → autocrine loop (eg, ↑ PDGF in brain tumors)
▘ Growth factor receptors → constitutive signaling (eg, HER2 in breast cancer)
▘ Signaling molecules (eg, RAS)
▘ Transcription factors (eg, MYC)
▘ Cell cycle regulators (eg, cyclins, CDKs)
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: HALLMARK 2 — Anti-growth signal insensitivity: mutations in tumor suppressor genes (eg, Rb); loss of E-cadherin function → loss of contact inhibition (eg, NF2 mutations)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Anti-growth signal
insensitivity

▘ Mutations in tumor suppressor genes (eg, Rb)
▘ Loss of E-cadherin function → loss of contact inhibition (eg, NF2 mutations)
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: HALLMARK 3 — Evasion of apoptosis: mutations in genes that regulate apoptosis (eg, TP53, BCL2 → follicular B cell lymphoma)

sourceEvidence.claim: HALLMARK 4 — Limitless replicative potential: reactivation of telomerase → maintenance and lengthening of telomeres → prevention of chromosome shortening and cell aging
sourceEvidence.quote:

sourceEvidence.claim: HALLMARK 5 — Sustained angiogenesis: ↑ pro-angiogenic factors (eg, VEGF) or ↓ inhibitory factors; factors may be produced by tumor or stromal cells; vessels can sprout from existing capillaries (neoangiogenesis) or endothelial cells are recruited from bone marrow (vasculogenesis); vessels may be leaky and/or dilated
sourceEvidence.quote:
Sustained
angiogenesis

↑ pro-angiogenic factors (eg, VEGF) or ↓ inhibitory factors. Factors may be produced by tumor or
stromal cells. Vessels can sprout from existing capillaries (neoangiogenesis) or endothelial cells are
recruited from bone marrow (vasculogenesis). Vessels may be leaky and/or dilated.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: HALLMARK 6 — Warburg effect: shift of glucose metabolism from mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation to glycolysis, even under aerobic conditions; driven by altered metabolic enzymes (eg, pyruvate kinase M2, LDH-A); aerobic glycolysis supplies rapidly dividing cancer cells with biosynthetic intermediates for nucleotide, lipid, and amino acid synthesis, resulting in ↑ lactate production
sourceEvidence.quote:
Warburg effect

Shift of glucose metabolism from mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation to glycolysis, even under
aerobic conditions. Driven by altered metabolic enzymes (eg, pyruvate kinase M2, LDH-A).
Aerobic glycolysis supplies rapidly dividing cancer cells with biosynthetic intermediates for
nucleotide, lipid, and amino acid synthesis, resulting in ↑ lactate production.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: HALLMARK 7 — Immune evasion in cancer: normally immune cells can recognize and attack tumor cells; for successful tumorigenesis, tumor cells must evade the immune system; multiple escape mechanisms exist
sourceEvidence.quote:
Immune evasion in
cancer

Normally, immune cells can recognize and attack tumor cells. For successful tumorigenesis, tumor
cells must evade the immune system. Multiple escape mechanisms exist:
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: HALLMARK 7 escape mechanism 1 — ↓ MHC class I expression by tumor cells → cytotoxic T cells are unable to recognize tumor cells
sourceEvidence.quote:

cells.

sourceEvidence.claim: HALLMARK 7 escape mechanism 2 — tumor cells secrete immunosuppressive factors (eg, TGF-β) and recruit regulatory T cells to downregulate immune response

sourceEvidence.claim: HALLMARK 7 escape mechanism 3 — tumor cells upregulate immune checkpoint molecules, which inhibit immune response

sourceEvidence.claim: HALLMARK 8 — Tissue invasion: loss of E-cadherin function → loosening of intercellular junctions → metalloproteinases degrade basement membrane and ECM → cells attach to ECM proteins (eg, laminin, fibronectin) → cells migrate through degraded ECM ('locomotion') → vascular dissemination
sourceEvidence.quote:
Tissue invasion

Loss of E-cadherin function → loosening of intercellular junctions → metalloproteinases degrade
basement membrane and ECM → cells attach to ECM proteins (eg, laminin, fibronectin) → cells
migrate through degraded ECM (“locomotion”) → vascular dissemination.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: HALLMARK 9 — Metastasis: tumor cells or emboli spread via lymphatics or blood → adhesion to endothelium → extravasation and homing; site of metastasis can be predicted by site of 1° tumor, as the target organ is often the first-encountered capillary bed; some cancers show organ tropism (eg, lung cancers commonly metastasize to adrenals)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Metastasis

Tumor cells or emboli spread via lymphatics or blood → adhesion to endothelium → extravasation
and homing. Site of metastasis can be predicted by site of 1° tumor, as the target organ is often the
first-encountered capillary bed. Some cancers show organ tropism (eg, lung cancers commonly
metastasize to adrenals).
